newsitem.title: JAPAN: Strong quake shakes southern Japan, damage unknown.
newsitem.headline: Strong quake shakes southern Japan, damage unknown.

text.p: Wide areas of Japan's southern island of Kyushu were rocked by a strong earthquake on Tuesday, the Meteorological Agency said.
The earthquake registered 6.1 on the Richter scale and was centred on Sendai in Kagoshima prefecture, about 985 km (615 miles) southwest of Tokyo, the agency said.
It struck at 2.38 p.m. (0538 GMT), shaking buildings in the prefectural capital of Kagoshima.
The tremor registered a six on the Japanese scale of seven, defined as a "violent tremor" which can be powerful enough to trigger landslides, open cracks in the ground and cause houses to collapse.
Authorities ordered all trains halted on Kyushu, the second-largest of Japan's four main islands, but there were no immediate reports of any casualties or damage.
There was no danger of tsunami tidal waves from the tremor, the agency said.

"No glass was broken but shelves fell over," said an official at the Sendai city hall contacted by phone by NHK public television. He added that there were no reports of any serious injuries at the city hall.
"There doesn't appear to be anything unusual," he said, although he added that the electricity was cut briefly.
The local power utility, Kyushu Electric Power Co Inc, said its nuclear power plant operations in the region were not affected by the earthquake.
"Our reactors are running normally, and there is no radiation leakage at the plants," a company spokesman said.
